newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises amid boosted demand.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises amid boosted demand.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate firmed to 10.1 percent on Friday from 8.7, as most lenders raised prices amid growing demand.
Dealers put the total daily trade at 55.5 million kuna against a demand of 70 million kuna, boosted by end-of-week corporate tax and pension payments.
Most settlements were fresh call money loans. Their weighted rate rose to 8.1 percent from 8.0 percent.
One-month money was granted at 15 percent and a smaller 10-day loan was made at 11 percent.
Insurers renewed old one-month loans at 12 percent, down from Thursday's 13 percent. Interbank term loans ranged between 15 percent for one-month funds and 16 to 19 percent for two-month borrowings.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates firmer at 6.2484 against the dollar and at 3.5699 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
